title: Job
hook: Before Job ever speaks a word of complaint, something happens that he never sees: a council convenes in heaven, and God himself invites the Adversary to give his report. That single detail reframes everything that follows—Job's agony is not a mystery to be solved but a drama already known above, unfolding on earth in real time while its meaning is contested in realms he cannot access. When Job finally opens his mouth in chapter 3, it isn't blasphemy that pours out but the rawest honesty scripture allows, the cry of a man who has kept faith yet still demands to understand. And when his friends answer with tidy theology—suffering as proof of sin—Job accuses them of something startling: lying for God, dressing up cruelty as piety. There's a reason Job's words still cut so close after three thousand years; few books in scripture take human pain this seriously, or trust the sufferer's voice this much. Come sit with Job a while—his questions may be the ones you've been afraid to ask, and his story might just make room for them.
